about: The `.kiao-files` grammar, as a table both implementations must agree on.
One syntax is read by two languages: Go, in worker, bounds the link fixer with it, and
Node, in the migration helpers, bounds what a migration may rewrite. Two readers of one grammar
drift unless something pins them together, and the cost of drift is asymmetric — a rule that
quietly matches less than it says lets an automatic rewrite reach a file the operator fenced
off. So the cases live here, once, and both test suites read them:
`declaration` is the whole file's text, `path` is relative to the folder that declared it, and
the two booleans are what each pass must decide about it.
`defaults` is what the root declaration says when a store has none of its own. worker
seeds it into a new store; the migration helpers fall back to it for a store that has never
been served. Both must mean the same thing, or a by-hand run would be bounded differently.

cases.name: a pattern without a slash matches at any depth
…including deep under the root
a directory match covers its contents
a name is matched whole, not as a prefix
a pattern containing a slash is anchored at the declaring folder
…and covers everything under it
…but not the same shape deeper down
a trailing slash is decoration, so the rule still matches at any depth
a leading slash anchors
…at the declaring folder
* matches within one segment
* does not cross a separator
a dot is a literal, not a wildcard
.* is how a declaration excludes dot-directories
…and leaves ordinary names alone
a line of just / covers the whole folder
comments and blank lines are not patterns
…and the pattern beside them still applies, trimmed
a pattern before any section bounds both passes
[migration] bounds migrations alone
[refactor] bounds link updates alone
an unknown section is parsed and never consulted
a section name is read case-insensitively
an empty declaration excludes nothing
